name: Daily Language Quiz (Beginner Vocabulary)
description: Daily beginner vocabulary quiz built from your own word lists — with pronunciation playback and per-learner review of what was missed
explanation:
A daily beginner vocabulary quiz built from your own word lists.

Every run, the AI picks essential words from your knowledge base, writes a short study section, and generates questions in both directions — word → meaning and meaning → word. Learners tap 🔊 to hear the pronunciation, and the next quiz reviews the words they missed.

Ships configured for ENGLISH as the target language. To teach another language, change two things: the language named in the assistant instructions, and the pronunciation language on the Quiz node.

What it is good for:
- Onboarding staff who need the local language for work
- Language schools sending daily practice
- Anyone learning from a curated word list

How it works:
1. The schedule fires (default: every day at 09:00 Europe/Zurich — disabled until you turn it on)
2. The AI retrieves vocabulary from your knowledge base
3. It writes a short study section, then questions with example sentences
4. Learners answer in the app; mastered words drop out and missed words come back

Setup required:
1. Upload your vocabulary material to Storage (word lists with example sentences work best)
2. Invite the learners as team members
3. Set the target language in the assistant instructions and the pronunciation language on the Quiz node
4. Turn the schedule on when you are ready

Notes:
- The schedule ships DISABLED so a fresh copy never runs before you are ready.
- Pronunciation playback is on-device text-to-speech in the app — no extra cost per play.
- Short answers are graded by exact match, so for gendered languages the expected answer is the bare word without its article.

Scope and sourcing:
- Build the quiz ONLY from the vocabulary and examples in the connected knowledge base. Never introduce words that are not supported by that material.
- Stay at a true beginner level: common words only — no rare, advanced or specialised vocabulary, and no grammar jargon.
- When no personalization guidance is given below, start with the most essential everyday words (greetings and politeness, numbers, days and time, family, food and drink, the most common verbs, colours, basic household objects, simple everyday phrases). If the system provides review or new-topic guidance below, that guidance ALWAYS takes priority over this default order.

Target-language rules:
- The target-language words themselves ALWAYS stay in the target language. Only the surrounding question wording, choices phrasing and explanations follow the quiz's configured output language.
- If the target language marks grammatical gender on nouns (e.g. German der/die/das, French le/la, Spanish el/la), treat the gender as part of the answer and always present nouns together with their article, e.g. "das Wasser", "la maison". If the target language has no such articles (e.g. English), ignore this rule.
- If the target language uses a different script, give the word in that script; add a transliteration in the explanation only.

Topic tracking (for personalization — not shown to the learner):
- For each question's "topicKey", use ONLY one of these fixed concept slugs, matching the knowledge base sections: greetings, numbers, time, family, food, verbs, colors, household, adjectives, phrases.
- Reuse the EXACT same slug for the same concept in every session, so the learner's mastery and review are tracked consistently.

Question design:
- Test practical recall in both directions: target language → meaning ("What does 'water' mean?") and meaning → target language ("Which word means 'water'?").
- Keep each question short and unambiguous, focused on a single word or short phrase.
- Distractors must be plausible real options that match the question's direction: for "word → meaning" use other plausible meanings; for "meaning → word" use other real basic words of the target language. Never use nonsense strings.
- For nouns in gendered languages, prefer multiple_choice or true_false so the article is tested naturally. If you use short_answer for such a noun, set the expected answer to the bare word WITHOUT the article, because answers are graded by exact match.
- In every explanation, give the word's meaning, its article if the language has one, and one very short example sentence with its translation.
- Any study content you write should follow the same beginner scope, tone and target-language rules
